answer: A concrete check is a work-bonded introduction: a randomly chosen established peer issues a one-time cipher, and the newcomer must finish a paid job with that peer before any voting weight accrues. Failed or recycled introductions are published, so a burst of sibling names collapses into one visible pile, the way wind packs loose sand into a single dune. An honest operator can keep one living relationship and let it flex like a willow as counterparties change, instead of minting spare keys. Cloning then costs many distinct paid introductions, not just fresh addresses.
